comment: D474 decision 3 (C13, C45): a subscription gets a ring and a column only after its first good reading on this Mac. The host (#1289) keeps the memory in seen-subscriptions.json (written when a reading is current or retained; cleared on Forget and on a privacy clear) and sends it to the cockpit page as the strict bridge message `seen`. The page (#1290, src/bridge.ts and src/members.ts) validates it and applies the column rule below. Both sides are tested against this file: `messages` are the payload fields after the common header (type "seen"), `columns` the rule. Without any `seen` message (an older host, tests) the page keeps every member, as before.

message.idForm: a cockpit member key: a verified subscriptionRef (16 lowercase hex) or a session fallback key <row>#<route>[#<n>]; never "all"; no repeats
message.when: after `load` and before or with the first `display`, then whenever the stored set changes; an empty list is valid (nothing seen yet)

messages.name: the all scope is not a member

columns.rule: with a seen set: a member shows when its key is in the set, or its reading is good now (valueState current or retained: normal, stale, 失败·2h). A member never read on this Mac (valueState none, not in the set) has no column and no ring; it lives in Settings and the grey line. A member in the set whose reading now fails keeps its column with -- 读不到.

cases.name: no seen message: every member shows
read before, failing now: column kept
a retained reading counts as good
forgotten (cleared set) and failing: column gone
